panel.summary: `allowed_bots` hardcodes a bot login (`yorkie-agent[bot]`) that is not tied to the App the workflows actually mint tokens for; a mismatch makes the guard a no-op and both fixer loops keep failing
panel.evidence: Both edits set `allowed_bots: "yorkie-agent[bot],yorkie-agent"`, but the App identity is entirely maintainer-supplied via `secrets.AGENT_APP_ID`/`AGENT_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` (agent-iterate-ci.yml:59-60, agent-review-panel.yml:373-374), and docs/tasks/active/20260720-autonomous-issue-to-pr-pipeline-todo.md:70-77 says the App may be "the Claude GitHub App **or a dedicated app**". The bot login that claude-code-action sees is the installed App's slug + `[bot]` (e.g. `claude[bot]`), which nothing in this repo pins to `yorkie-agent`. If the configured App has any other slug, the allow-list does not match, claude-code-action still refuses the bot-initiated run, and the fix step keeps failing — i.e. the stated bug is not fixed and (via the new `needs: fix` branch) every blocked PR now ends in a human page instead. There is no verification step or documented prerequisite forcing the App slug to be `yorkie-agent`.
